correctness.rationale: Independently obtained the coefficient by the periodic diagonal gauge x=e^{TH}v in phase time. The gauged generator is T(A0+T[A0,H]+T²[[A0,H],H]/2+O(T³)). The period mean of [A0,H] vanishes. In the normalized periodic profile the order-T term is constant and the next solvability condition makes it zero along with the linear exponent term. Pairing the order-T³ solvability condition with q kills A0−λ0I, leaving exactly the stated edge sum; [[A0,H],H]_{ij}=L_{ij}(H_j−H_i)² off diagonal. Bounded coefficients give a convergent fundamental-matrix power series, and the simple eigenvalue of the analytic desingularized monodromy fixes the branch at zero, justifying the differentiated remainder. Connectivity forces common H at zero energy; the resulting common scalar forcing factors out exactly at every period. Equality and differences of forcing must be understood a.e. (values at individual discontinuities are immaterial, as in the definition of H). In a separate exact directed three-cycle example with durations 1/4 and 3/4 and rates (1,2,4) and −(1,2,4)/3, the common zero-mean primitive factor has variance 1/192 and the coefficient is 7/576. This is an exact coefficient check, not a direct monodromy simulation. The frozen reported 36 assertions were inspected, not rerun.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Conservative migration is already included. For n=2, split patch 2 into two identical patches, giving each half the 1-to-2 inflow, the original per-capita outflow to 1, and the same seasonal rates. The lifted system is strongly connected and intertwines by J(x1,x2)=(x1,x2/2,x2/2). The positive lifted monodromy eigenvector is principal, and the lifted Perron weights with q'=(q1,q2,q2) give the identical energy, summing the duplicate edges. The d≥3 restriction therefore does not leave a distinct two-patch finding.
